title: 190. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Classifying Consistency of Linear Systems
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Classifying consistency of a linear system by comparing slopes
questions.learningObjective: Identify an inconsistent linear system whose lines are parallel and distinct.
questions.question: Classify the system \(y=2x+1,\quad y=2x-3\).

options.label: A
options.text: The system is consistent and has exactly one solution.

options.label: B
options.text: The system is inconsistent and has no solution.

questions.explanation: Both equations are in slope-intercept form with slope \(2\). The \(y\)-intercepts are \(1\) and \(-3\), so the lines are parallel and distinct. Parallel distinct lines never intersect, so the system has no solution and is inconsistent.
questions.hint: Compare the slopes and \(y\)-intercepts of the two lines.

questions.concept: Classifying consistency of a linear system by recognizing equivalent equations
questions.learningObjective: Identify a consistent dependent linear system that has infinitely many solutions.
questions.question: Classify the system \(x+y=4,\quad 2x+2y=8\).

options.label: A
options.text: The system is inconsistent and has no solution.

options.label: B
options.text: The system is consistent and has infinitely many solutions.

questions.explanation: The second equation is obtained by multiplying the first equation by \(2\): \(2(x+y)=2(4)\), which gives \(2x+2y=8\). The two equations represent the same line, so every point on the line is a solution. Therefore, the system has infinitely many solutions.
questions.hint: Check whether one equation is a multiple of the other.

questions.concept: Classifying consistency by comparing coefficient and constant ratios
questions.learningObjective: Determine that a linear system is inconsistent when coefficient ratios are equal but constant ratios differ.
questions.question: Classify the system \(2x+3y=6,\quad 4x+6y=10\).

options.label: A
options.text: The system is consistent and has exactly one solution.

options.label: B
options.text: The system is inconsistent and has no solution.

questions.explanation: Compare the ratios of the coefficients: \(\frac{2}{4}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}\). The ratio of the constants is \(\frac{6}{10}=\frac{3}{5}\), which is not equal to \(\frac{1}{2}\). Since the coefficient ratios are equal but the constant ratios are not, the lines are parallel and distinct. The system has no solution and is inconsistent.
questions.hint: Compare the ratios of the \(x\)-coefficients, \(y\)-coefficients, and constants.

questions.concept: Classifying consistency by recognizing proportional equations
questions.learningObjective: Determine that a linear system is consistent and dependent when one equation is a multiple of the other.
questions.question: Classify the system \(x+2y=3,\quad 3x+6y=9\).

options.label: A
options.text: The system is inconsistent and has no solution.

options.label: B
options.text: The system is consistent and has infinitely many solutions.

questions.explanation: The second equation is \(3\) times the first equation: \(3(x+2y)=3(3)\), which gives \(3x+6y=9\). The equations represent the same line, so the system is consistent and dependent. It has infinitely many solutions.
questions.hint: Divide the second equation by \(3\) and compare it with the first equation.

questions.concept: Using elimination to classify a linear system
questions.learningObjective: Use elimination to recognize a dependent linear system with infinitely many solutions.
questions.question: Use elimination to classify the system \(2x-3y=4,\quad 4x-6y=8\).

options.label: A
options.text: The system is consistent and has infinitely many solutions.

options.label: B
options.text: The system is inconsistent and has no solution.

questions.explanation: Multiply the first equation by \(2\): \(4x-6y=8\). This is exactly the second equation. Therefore, the two equations represent the same line, and the system is consistent and dependent. It has infinitely many solutions.
questions.hint: Multiply the first equation by \(2\) and compare the result with the second equation.

questions.concept: Finding a parameter value that makes a linear system inconsistent
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of a parameter for which a linear system has no solution.
questions.question: For what value of \(k\) is the system \(x+ky=3,\quad 2x+4y=5\) inconsistent?
questions.explanation: For the system to be inconsistent, the lines must be parallel and distinct. This requires \(\frac{1}{2}=\frac{k}{4}\) and \(\frac{1}{2}\ne \frac{3}{5}\). From \(\frac{1}{2}=\frac{k}{4}\), we get \(k=2\). Checking the constant ratio, \(\frac{3}{5}\ne \frac{1}{2}\), so the system is indeed inconsistent when \(k=2\).
questions.hint: For an inconsistent system, the coefficients must be proportional but the constants must not be.

questions.concept: Finding a parameter value that makes a linear system dependent
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of a parameter for which a linear system has infinitely many solutions.
questions.question: For what value of \(k\) does the system \(3x+2y=6,\quad kx+4y=12\) have infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation:
For infinitely many solutions, the two equations must represent the same line, so their coefficients and constants must be proportional:
\[
\frac{3}{k}=\frac{2}{4}=\frac{6}{12}
\]
Since \(\frac{2}{4}=\frac{1}{2}\) and \(\frac{6}{12}=\frac{1}{2}\), we need \(\frac{3}{k}=\frac{1}{2}\). Thus \(k=6\).
questions.hint: Set up equal ratios for the \(x\)-coefficients, \(y\)-coefficients, and constants.

questions.concept: Classifying consistency by rewriting equations in slope-intercept form
questions.learningObjective: Determine that a linear system is inconsistent by identifying parallel distinct lines.
questions.question: Classify the system \(x-y=1,\quad 2x-2y=5\).

options.label: A
options.text: The system is inconsistent and has no solution.

options.label: B
options.text: The system is consistent and has exactly one solution.

questions.explanation: Rewrite the first equation as \(y=x-1\). Divide the second equation by \(2\): \(x-y=\frac{5}{2}\), so \(y=x-\frac{5}{2}\). Both lines have slope \(1\), but their \(y\)-intercepts are \(-1\) and \(-\frac{5}{2}\), which are different. The lines are parallel and distinct, so the system has no solution and is inconsistent.
questions.hint: Write both equations in the form \(y=mx+b\) and compare their slopes and intercepts.

questions.concept: Classifying consistency using coefficient and constant ratios
questions.learningObjective: Analyze a linear system to determine that it is inconsistent.
questions.question: Classify the system \(3x-2y=5,\quad 4y=6x-7\).

options.label: A
options.text: The system is inconsistent and has no solution.

options.label: B
options.text: The system is consistent and has infinitely many solutions.

questions.explanation: Rewrite the second equation in standard form: \(6x-4y=7\). The coefficients are proportional because \(\frac{3}{6}=\frac{-2}{-4}=\frac{1}{2}\). However, the constants are not in the same ratio: \(\frac{5}{7}\ne \frac{1}{2}\). Therefore, the two lines are parallel and distinct. The system has no solution and is inconsistent.
questions.hint: Write both equations in the form \(ax+by=c\), then compare the ratio of the coefficients with the ratio of the constants.

questions.concept: Finding a parameter value for a dependent linear system
questions.learningObjective: Determine the parameter value that makes two linear equations represent the same line.
questions.question: For the system \(x+2y=5,\quad 3x+6y=k\), which value of \(k\) gives infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation: For infinitely many solutions, the second equation must be a multiple of the first. Since \(3(x+2y)=3x+6y\) and \(3(5)=15\), the second equation must be \(3x+6y=15\). Therefore, \(k=15\).
questions.hint: For infinitely many solutions the two equations must describe the same line, so the coefficients and the constants must be in the same ratio.
